\caption{Accounting for every closed-loop dose attempt in both test rounds, by powder and target mass. \emph{Attempts} counts every dose the controller started. A dose is \emph{valid} when its run passed screening, it ended in a defined controller state, and the auger or solenoid moved (a continuous spin in the bulk phase counts even when it was too short for the firmware's 1~s clock to log a revolution). \emph{Within limit} counts valid doses inside the acceptance limit ($\pm$10\% at 50~mg, $\pm$5\% at 200~mg and 1~g). The firmware columns give the controller's own end label for each valid dose. \emph{ok}: inside its $\pm$5~mg stopping band; \emph{over}: more than 5~mg above the target; \emph{stall}: the reading stopped rising; \emph{budget}: 200 cycles of one phase; \emph{time}: 900~s. The controller stopped on its own $\pm$5~mg band, whereas doses are scored against the acceptance limit, so the two counts differ. At 1~g, for example, 9 of the 18 doses labelled stalled were within the $\pm$50~mg limit. The two indented rows split the 1~g total by powder. The 24 doses within the limit are every dose on the seven fastest-flowing powders dosed (24 of 24): AlSi10Mg, coarse silicon, sodium sulfate, calcium lactate, xanthan gum, NaCl, and CMC. The 15 valid doses on the other four (white rice flour, sodium alginate, fine silicon, and brown rice flour) all missed it. The last column gives the reason for each excluded attempt, with the number of attempts, or why a combination was not run. One valid 200~mg calcium lactate dose was reconstructed from its balance trace and camera record after the serial link failed. Powders are in the order of Table~1 of the main text. Per-dose records are in \texttt{paper/figures/data/doses\_all.csv}.}\label{tbl:doseaccount}\\
